text.p: Brisbane stock broker Wilson HTM Ltd said it was "probably prudent" for investors to view Papua New Guinea (PNG) mining and oil investor Orogen Minerals Ltd as a "hold" during the current political turmoils in PNG.
But this current view did not alter Wilson's long-term outlook about the company's potential, senior resource analyst John Webby told Reuters on Tuesday.
"It probably is prudent to hold Orogen in the face of current uncertainties but this does not change our long-term view of the potential of Orogen," Webby said.
"Orogen's projected growth in oil revenues over the next three years provide significant upside," Webby said in a report, published before the current unheaval in Papua New Guinea.
Production from Gobe and SE Gobe (Orogen 20.5 percent) was due to come on stream during the third quarter of 1998 which was additional to interim production from Moran 1X due late this year, he said.
These projects included the development of the greater Moran structure over the next two years and had the potential to double Orogen's current level of oil production.

In addition, there was the long-term value in the option agreement Orogen had with the PNG goverment which allowed the group to purchase 20.5 percent equity in any major petroleum project or 25 percent of any major mining project in PNG, Webby said in his report.
At the time of the report, Orogen' share price was A$3.42. Orogen's share price stood at A$3.22 a 11.30 a.m. (0030 GMT).
Wilson HTM forecast Orogen's net profit for calendar 1997 at A$52.2 million. Orogen posted a net profit of A$18 million for 1996, which included only four months of operations.
This was above the prospectus forecast of A$12 million.
Wilson forecast net profit would rise to A$72.4 million in 1998.
